Fragmentation.description:
Whether, and how, the acquisition fragmented its ions.

An MS/MS imaging run measures fragments, so the m/z axis of the table
means fragment m/z. Nothing about the axis says so, which is why this
block exists: without it an MS/MS store is indistinguishable from an
MS1 one.

The MSI table sums a frame that isolated several precursors into one
spectrum. ``merges_precursors`` says when that has happened, so a
consumer knows the spectrum is a chimera rather than discovering it
from the peaks, and ``resolved_table`` names the sibling table that
holds those precursors split apart when one was written.

constant_across_pixels.description: Whether every pixel was fragmented on the same schedule. A scheduled method makes it so; a data-dependent one does not, and then the windows below are not a global precursor axis.
constant_across_pixels.title: Constant Across Pixels

merges_precursors.description: Whether one stored spectrum sums fragments of more than one precursor, so its peaks cannot be attributed to a single one.
merges_precursors.title: Merges Precursors

ms_level.description: MS level of the stored spectra: 1 for a survey scan.
ms_level.title: Ms Level

present.description: True when the stored spectra are fragment spectra.
present.title: Present

resolved_table.description: Element key of the demultiplexed sibling table (pixels x (precursor, fragment)) written beside this summed table, when one was.
resolved_table.title: Resolved Table

windows.description: The precursor schedule, empty when none was reported.
windows.title: Windows

Fragmentation.title: Fragmentation

IonMobility.description:
Whether, and how, the acquisition separated ions by mobility.

Written so a consumer can tell a spectrum that was *summed over* a
mobility ramp (Bruker TDF, TIMS engaged) from one that never had a
mobility dimension (TSF, imzML, most other sources).  The MSI table
Thyra writes collapses the ramp; the fields here describe what was
collapsed.  Mobility is a spectral coordinate, never a spatial one,
so nothing about it appears in the store's coordinate systems.

grid.description: The common mobility grid the resolved table was binned onto, when it was built from per-pixel mobility values.

num_scans.description: Mobility scans per frame (the TIMS ramp length); the largest when frames differ.
num_scans.title: Num Scans

present.description: True when the source carries a mobility dimension, e.g. a Bruker TDF acquisition with TIMS engaged.
present.title: Present

range_lower.description: Lower bound of the acquired mobility range.
range_lower.title: Range Lower

range_upper.description: Upper bound of the acquired mobility range.
range_upper.title: Range Upper

resolved_table.description: Element key of the mobility-resolved sibling table (pixels x (m/z, mobility)) written beside this summed table, when one was.
resolved_table.title: Resolved Table

separation.description: The mobility quantity the instrument records, e.g. 'inverse reduced ion mobility' (TIMS) or 'ion mobility drift time'.
separation.title: Separation

separation_term.description: PSI-MS term for the quantity: MS:1002815 (inverse reduced ion mobility) or MS:1002476 (ion mobility drift time).

unit_term.description: Unit of range_lower and range_upper, e.g. MS:1002814 volt-second per square centimeter for 1/K0.

IonMobility.title: IonMobility

IsolationWindow.description:
One precursor isolation, named the way mzPeak names it.

The window spans ``[target - lower_offset, target + upper_offset]``.
Offsets rather than a single width is mzPeak's shape (and mzML's);
a source reporting one full width has it halved into two equal
offsets, which is the reading every mzML writer for those
instruments takes.

lower_offset.description: How far below the target the window reaches, in m/z.
lower_offset.title: Lower Offset

scan_begin.description: First mobility scan this window occupies, when the source separates its windows along the mobility ramp (Bruker PASEF).
scan_begin.title: Scan Begin

scan_end.description: One past the last mobility scan this window occupies.
scan_end.title: Scan End

upper_offset.description: How far above the target the window reaches, in m/z.
upper_offset.title: Upper Offset

IsolationWindow.title: IsolationWindow

MSAnalysis.description:
How the data was acquired (METASPACE ``MS_Analysis``).

``pixel_size_um`` is the one field that is always known at
conversion time (conversion refuses to run without a pixel size),
so it is the one required field of the section.

detector_resolving_power.description: Resolving power at a reference m/z.

fragmentation.description: Whether the stored spectra are fragment spectra and, if so, of which precursors; unset when the source does not say.

instrument_model.description: Instrument model as reported by the source.
instrument_model.title: Instrument Model

ion_mobility.description: Whether the source separated ions by mobility and, if so, over what range; the MSI table is summed over that dimension.

MSAnalysis.title: MSAnalysis

MobilityGrid.description:
The common mobility grid a mobility-resolved table was binned onto.

Describes the channels of a grid table (pixels x (m/z, mobility)
built from per-pixel mobility sources): the law the channel edges
follow, the range they span and how many there are. Absent until
such a table is written; the store's ``uns["mobility_heatmap"]`` uses
the same channel count and edges so the two align by index.

law.description: How channel edges are spaced across the range, e.g. 'linear' (equal width in the axis unit).
law.title: Law

lower.description: Lower edge of the first channel.
lower.title: Lower

upper.description: Upper edge of the last channel.
upper.title: Upper

MobilityGrid.title: MobilityGrid

OntologyTerm.description: A controlled-vocabulary reference: CURIE accession plus label.

name.description: The term's primary label in its ontology.
name.title: Name

OntologyTerm.title: OntologyTerm

x.description: Pixel size along x in micrometres.
x.title: X

y.description: Pixel size along y in micrometres.
y.title: Y

ProcessingStep.description:
One processing action between the raw data and this store.

Modeled on mzQC provenance: an ordered list of steps, each naming
the software that performed it and the parameters it ran with.  The
converter records its own steps (conversion, mass axis resampling);
downstream tools append theirs (normalisation, peak picking,
annotation) when they modify the store.

name.description: What was done, e.g. 'conversion', 'mass axis resampling', 'normalisation', 'peak picking', 'annotation'.
name.title: Name

parameters.description: The parameters the step ran with.
parameters.title: Parameters

ProcessingStep.title: ProcessingStep

Provenance.description:
Who wrote the block and from what.

Deliberately small: the store's ``uns["essential_metadata"]`` and
root attributes already record dimensions, mass range, spectrum
type and conversion timestamp.  This section records only what is
needed to interpret the *metadata block itself*, and contains no
timestamps so that two conversions of the same input produce an
identical block (the uns parity tests rely on this).

pixel_size_source.description: How the pixel size was determined: read from the source metadata ('automatic'), supplied by the user ('manual'), or the 1.0 um fallback ('default').
pixel_size_source.title: Pixel Size Source

source_path.description: Path of the source data at conversion time.
source_path.title: Source Path

thyra_version.description: Thyra version that wrote the block.
thyra_version.title: Thyra Version

Provenance.title: Provenance

ResolvingPower.description: Mass resolving power quoted at a reference m/z.

at_mz.description: The m/z the value is quoted at.
at_mz.title: At Mz

ResolvingPower.title: ResolvingPower

organism_part_term.description: UBERON term for the organism part.

matrix.description: MALDI matrix, e.g. '2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid (DHB)'. 'none' for matrix-free techniques (DESI, SIMS).
matrix.title: Matrix

matrix_term.description: CHEBI term for the matrix compound.

SoftwareRef.description: A software agent, the way mzQC records analysis software.
SoftwareRef.title: SoftwareRef

description:
The versioned MSI metadata document.

``sample`` and ``preparation`` cannot be auto-populated from raw
files and default to empty; ``ms_analysis`` and ``provenance`` are
written by the converter for every store.

ms_analysis.description: How the data was acquired; auto-populated where possible.

preparation.description: How the sample was prepared; user-supplied.

provenance.description: Who wrote this block and from what source.
